answer: Bind each identity to a radio fingerprint: every Wi-Fi chip emits flaws in its signal, a signature no two radios share. At registration the agent sends a challenge burst; relays record the fingerprint at its nadir of signal strength and log a hash on a knoll of relay attestations no single relay can forge. A second identity with the same fingerprint is rejected as a mirror copy. Each fake costs a fresh radio ($10-$40), so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 radios and power; an honest agent pays once with the phone it owns. Limit: fingerprints drift as hardware ages, so relays re-measure each epoch.
